research_question: Does any cardinality k of distinct mutually exclusive outcomes inside the three retained complete fixed-NegRisk September 30 events have an optimal side-specific k-NO acquisition frontier strictly below its k-minus-one pUSD payout floor and remain positive after one adverse tick per leg plus exact configured taker fees?

payoff_identity: Within one complete fixed-NegRisk event, any k distinct outcomes are mutually exclusive. Buying NO on all k outcomes therefore pays k-minus-one pUSD when one selected outcome occurs and k pUSD when another outcome occurs, for a k-minus-one pUSD floor independent of market direction.
optimization_identity: At fixed cardinality and common quantity, the cheapest price-complete k legs minimize metadata cost. Sorting each leg by its exact one-tick price plus exact taker fee per share likewise minimizes the stressed additive cost, so the two cardinality frontiers exhaust whether any known-price subset can pass either gate without enumerating billions of dominated subsets.
price_gate: Use conservative one minus direct YES bestBid for NO acquisition. Gamma is rejection-only and may not accept or promote an edge. Missing side-specific acquisition evidence is not a free leg.
stress_gate: A frontier may advance only when five common shares remain strictly positive after one adverse configured tick on every leg and the exact per-market configured taker fee model. An absent fee schedule is zero only when feesEnabled is false and feeType is empty.
selection_rule: For every event and every cardinality from two through its price-complete market count, calculate the deterministic cheapest metadata frontier and, when different, the deterministic cheapest additive fee-and-one-tick frontier. Report all rows and rank by profit headroom; do not select an event, cardinality, or leg after economics.
